chapter: Opinions on pop music, jazz education and the business
title: Jazz programs in American colleges
summary: Wilson lists jazz departments at Ohio State, Eastman, Indiana, North Texas and others, including thirty-piece school bands he judged.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well, what do you think the school system should do? Considering jazz, Teddy?

Well, I think that they are encouraging things. Now Ohio State has a jazz department that's just five years old now, a big jazz department, they started it. The Eastman Conservatory in Rochester has a jazz department that's about five or six years old, and Alan Dawson is very enthusiastic about it, he was out there doing a seminar a few years ago, and he was raving to me about their department.

The University of Indiana has jazz, and Steven was mentioning about North Texas State. They played in some of George Wein's festivals, the number one band, you know, down in Austin, Texas, and those guys sounded like Woody Herman or Maynard Ferguson, a Buddy Rich type band. And just ten of those big twenty-piece jazz bands, all at one time, and the number one band on down, in those days, and I think the University of Nebraska has a big Ashford jazz course, that guy, Alexander, he was up there for awhile, did you know that? When he left North Texas State, and now he's with a big school out in California.

So all these schools are training a lot of jazz people and then others -- I was just down in Dallas or Houston, a few years ago, to help judge these bands, some school bands. Max Kaminsky was down there, and Jimmy Owens, and quite a few professional players, and they had 30-piece jazz bands. They were using seven trumpets and six trombones,

with a tuba, seven reeds and all sorts of -- a 30 piece jazz band, playing arrangements and originals. And some of them were from Houston, the University of Texas in Austin, and University of all those southern schools got jazz departments. ^ Alabama, you know -- all the southern schools have jazz bands in them.
Then there is hope for us, right?

I know -- I'm a friend of a man who heads jazz studies at the University of South Carolina, he used to be head of jazz at the University of Texas, in Austin, he's down in South Carolina now, and he plays all the instruments, and bass is his specialty.

So it's there in all of these schools. This jazz music, teaching them -- playing in these big bands and taking courses. But Berklee is going further in teaching them the whole business -- everything except to equip a guy to play in the symphony. You can't go out of Berklee and join the symphony. But you're on the road, and you got the fundamentals, and maybe you can go on to New England if you want to sit in the Boston Symphony and play, but if you want to sit in a Hollywood band or a recording studio or sit in on a session or play with Buddy Rich's band, or even play in a rock band -- do they teach that?
